intro.title: @keyframes and animation
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple animated element, like a bouncing ball or a fading box, to bring your web pages to life. You will learn the core concept of defining custom animations using the @keyframes rule, which lets you specify exactly how an element's style changes over time. The main technologies involved are the @keyframes rule to create the animation sequence and the animation property to apply it to an element. By the end, you'll be able to create smooth, eye-catching animations using pure CSS.
intro.usecase: The @keyframes and animation properties are essential for creating smooth, engaging UI feedback and transitions in modern web applications. For example, developers use them to animate loading spinners on dashboards, highlight new notifications with a subtle pulse, or create smooth slide-in effects for modals and side panels. These animations enhance user experience by providing visual cues, guiding attention, and making interfaces feel more responsive and polished. Mastering CSS animations allows you to implement common patterns like progress bars, hover effects on buttons, and attention-grabbing alerts without relying on heavy JavaScript libraries.
